note: A retirement is a preservation claim, not a story about a red run. Every entry registers the retired path (file), the original path it was retired from (original_path), the sha256 of the preserved bytes (the retirement's retired_sha256), the commit those bytes are claimed to come from (retired_from_commit), a free-text reason, the registration date (retired_on) and the review that accepted the retirement (review_reference). scripts/verify-retirement-registry.js reads no test output. It checks five things from files, hashes and the object store: (a) preserved - the file at the registered path hashes to the registered sha256; (b) complete - every file under tests/legacy/ is registered; (c) not a fake retirement - the original path does not still carry the registered bytes; (d) re-evaluable - the registered bytes are put back at the original path and run, and a passing run is named as a receipt (KDNA-RETIREMENT-RESTORABLE) because the entry is not stale; (e) zero rewrite - the copy under tests/legacy/ is byte for byte the file that was at the original path. Which commit that means is pinned by the gate, not trusted to the entry: the retirement commit is the newest commit that removes the file from its original location while its parent carries exactly the registered bytes, retired_from_commit must be that commit's parent verbatim, the registered sha256 must be that parent's blob at original_path as read from the object store, and that parent must not itself be the commit that wrote those bytes (a rewrite in the commit immediately before the move is refused). Only (a)-(c) and (e) decide the exit code. Each retired copy here is the pre-retirement file itself: the move into tests/legacy/ changed nothing, not even a relative require or a path resolved from __dirname, because nothing under tests/legacy/ is ever run. The suites are red against the committed graph because the objects they exercise are gone from it; that is recorded as an independent observation in the delivery report, and a file that would only fit tests/legacy/ after being adapted is not retired at all.
